text: Everything you've seen so far is experimental facts quantum mechanics has to explain. The postulates are the actual rulebook — five precise statements that define what quantum mechanics is as a mathematical theory.

Postulate one: every physical state is a normalized vector in a Hilbert space. For a single qubit, that's psi equals a ket-zero plus b ket-one, with the magnitude of a squared plus the magnitude of b squared equal to 1. That vector is the complete description — nothing requires a hidden classical value underneath it. Postulate two: every measurable quantity is represented by a Hermitian operator, which is guaranteed to have only real-number eigenvalues — because a measured quantity like energy or a bit value has to come out real, not complex.

Postulate three: measuring returns one of that operator's eigenvalues, never anything in between, with probability given by the Born rule — the squared magnitude of the relevant amplitude. Postulate four: immediately after measuring, the state collapses to the eigenstate matching whatever outcome you actually got. Measure again right away in the same basis, and you'll get that same result with certainty, because the superposition that could have produced a different answer is simply gone.

Here's the Born rule made concrete. Take psi equals 0.6 ket-zero plus 0.8 ket-one — normalized, since 0.6 squared plus 0.8 squared equals 1. The probability of measuring 0 is 0.6 squared, which is 0.36; the probability of measuring 1 is 0.8 squared, which is 0.64; and those sum to exactly 1, as they must. If the outcome comes out 1, the state immediately collapses to exactly ket-one — every trace of the ket-zero component is gone for good.

Postulate five: as long as a system is closed — not being measured — it evolves smoothly and deterministically via a unitary operator, which always preserves normalization and is always reversible. This is exactly why every quantum logic gate is a unitary matrix. Read together, the five postulates tell a complete story: postulate one is what a qubit's state is, postulate five is what a gate does to it, and postulates two through four are what happens when you read it out. There's no sixth postulate hiding anything else.
